shadow:
There is a kind of tired that sleep does not fix. You wake up already spent. The day has not asked anything of you yet and the tank is somehow low. This is not the honest tiredness of a body that worked well. It is the wear of a body running on borrowed reserves, pushing at something that does not want to move.

Most of the time it comes from force. Force looks like will, but it is will pointed the wrong way. You keep a job that gives your spirit no room. You say yes to a person who never really sees you. You push your life against its own current and call that discipline. The current does not care. It takes the energy back, slowly, and the body pays the bill in the stomach and the sleep and the flat grey feeling under everything.

People treat this as a flaw in their stamina, something to caffeine through. That is the wrong read. The exhaustion is not weakness. It is a signal, accurate and patient, telling you exactly where your life and your true direction have come apart. It wants you to stop pushing the thing that was never yours to push.
repressive: Some people answer the tiredness by giving way. They let others draw on them without limit, decide their needs were always smaller than everyone else's, and pour themselves out for people who will not notice when the well runs dry.
reactive: Others answer it by hardening. They drive themselves and the people near them, keep everyone at arm's length, and run on a will fed by old anger. They look unstoppable. The cost is hidden, and it is steep.
gift:
The same force that wore you down is the force that, turned right, fills you back up. Nothing about the energy changes. Only the direction does. When your life lines up with its real current, you find there is far more available than you ever had while pushing.

Resolve begins with a small word. No. It is the ability to put a boundary around your own energy and hold it there. When you say no to the wrong thing, you are not closing a door, you are letting that thing go find where it actually belongs.

This is also the gift of doing nothing well. Rest recharges the body. Real relaxation reaches lower than that, into the parts of you that rest alone cannot touch. People with resolve still work hard, sometimes very hard, but the work does not drain them, because they are no longer forcing it. The will is already inside the task. It pours out instead of being squeezed.

And it likes solitude. Resolve grows in the quiet, in the hours that belong to you and no one else. Something in you keeps producing, keeps refilling, and a person fed from inside like that draws others without needing them.
siddhi:
Here the boundary stops being something you set and becomes something you simply are. There is no more pushing, because there is no longer anyone standing apart from life, deciding what to push.

This is the strange one. The masters who arrive through this code are the ones who deny that you need a path at all. They will tell you there is no God to find outside your own aloneness, that the search itself is the last thing in the way. It sounds like a closed door. It is the opposite. The seeking was the final effort, the final force, and when it drops there is nothing left between you and what was always here.

What remains is complete physical relaxation. Not slackness. Every cell of you tuned and unhindered, the body finally let go of a tension it carried for so long it forgot it was carrying it. From here you can look back at the exhaustion at the start and see it was never punishment. It was the current, faithful all along, refusing to let you settle anywhere that was not yours.
